questions.q: Who is it that guards Daniel’s people?
questions.a: Michael, the great prince, guards Daniel’s people.

questions.q: How bad will the time of trouble be?
questions.a: It will be a time of trouble such as never was since the beginning of any nation until that time.

questions.q: At that time who will be saved?
questions.a: At that time Daniel’s people will be saved, everyone whose name is found written in the book.

questions.q: What will happen to many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth?
questions.a: Some of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will rise up to everlasting life, and some will rise up to shame and everlasting contempt.

questions.q: What will happen to those who are wise and those who turn many to righteousness?
questions.a: Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the sky above, and those who turn many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.

questions.q: How long was Daniel told to keep the book sealed?
questions.a: He was told to keep the book sealed until the time of the end.

questions.q: Who did Daniel see standing beside the river?
questions.a: Daniel saw two other men, one standing on each side of the river.

questions.q: What did one of the two men ask the man clothed in linen?
questions.a: He asked how long it would be until the end of these wonders.

questions.q: How long did the man clothed in linen say it would be until the end of these amazing events?
questions.a: The man clothed in linen said it would be for a time, times, and a half. When the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things will be completed.

questions.q: What did Daniel ask after he heard but did not understand?
questions.a: Daniel asked what would be the end of these things.

questions.q: What did the man clothed in linen say when Daniel told him he did not understand?
questions.a: The man clothed in linen said to Daniel, “Go your way, Daniel, for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.”

questions.q: At the time of the end, who will and who will not understand the words of the prophecy?
questions.a: None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.

questions.q: How much time will elapse between the time that the perpetual sacrifice is removed and the abomination that causes desolation is set up?
questions.a: There will be 1,290 days between those two events.

questions.q: At that time who does the man clothed in linen say will be blessed?
questions.a: The man clothed in linen said, “Blessed is the one who waits until the end of the 1,335 days.”

questions.q: What did the man clothed in linen say would happen to Daniel?
questions.a: He said that Daniel would rest and that he would rise for his reward at the end of days.

commentary.text: The conclusion of the vision of the Scriptures of truth. (Dan. 12:1-4) The times of the continuance of these events. (Dan. 12:5-13)

Dan. 12:1-4. Michael signifies, "Who is like God," and his name, with the title of "the great Prince," points out the Divine Saviour. Christ stood for the children of our people in their stead as a sacrifice, bore the curse for them, to bear it from them. He stands for them in pleading for them at the throne of grace. And after the destruction of antichrist, the Lord Jesus shall stand at the latter day upon the earth; and He shall appear for the complete redemption of all his people. When God works deliverance from persecution for them, it is as life from the dead. When his gospel is preached, many who sleep in the dust, both Jews and Gentiles, shall be awakened by it out of their heathenism of Judaism. And in the end the multitude that sleep in the dust shall awake; many shall arise to life, and many to shame. There is glory reserved for all the saints in the future state, for all that are wise, wise for their souls and eternity. Those who turn many to righteousness, who turn sinners from the errors of their ways, and help to save their souls from death, James 5:20, will share in the glory of those they have helped to heaven, which will add to their own glory.

Dan. 12:5-13 One of the angels asking how long it should be to the end of these wonders, a solemn reply is made, that it would be for a time, times, and a half, the period mentioned Dan. 7:25, and in the Revelation. It signifies 1260 prophetic days or years, beginning from the time when the power of the holy people should be scattered. The imposture of Mohammed, and the papal usurpation, began about the same time; and these were a twofold attack upon the church of God. But all will end well at last. All opposing rule, principality, and power, shall be put down, and holiness and love will triumph, and be in honour, to eternity. The end, this end, shall come. What an amazing prophecy is this, of so many varied events, and extending through so many successive ages, even to the general resurrection! Daniel must comfort himself with the pleasing prospect of his own happiness in death, in judgment, and to eternity. It is good for us all to think much of going away from this world. That must be our way; but it is our comfort that we shall not go till God calls us to another world, and till he has done with us in this world; till he says, Go thou thy way, thou hast done thy work, therefore now, go thy way, and leave it to others to take thy place. It was a comfort to Daniel, and is a comfort to all the saints, that whatever their lot is in the days of their lives, they shall have a happy lot in the end of the days. And it ought to be the great care and concern of every one of us to secure this. Then we may well be content with our present lot, and welcome the will of God. Believers are happy at all times; they rest in God by faith now, and a rest is reserved for them in heaven at last.
